question: What curved spacetime really means

scene.title: What curved spacetime really means
scene.subtitle: Straight paths that start side by side don’t stay side by side. That is what curved spacetime means, and it explains the tides.
scene.takeaway: Spacetime is curved where floating paths that start side by side come together or spread apart. Mass draws them together.

beats.title: Straight lines that meet
beats.body: Two walkers start side by side on a ball, facing the same way, and walk straight ahead. Neither ever turns, yet they get closer and meet. On a curved surface, straight paths that start parallel come together.

beats.title: Falling side by side
beats.body: Now let go of two balls side by side, high above the Earth. Neither is pushed, and both start at rest. Far from any planet, they would stay the same distance apart forever. Near Earth they drift together as they fall, like the walkers: that is curved spacetime.

beats.title: Around the Earth
beats.body: Now let go of a ring of balls all around the Earth. The whole ring shrinks: the Earth’s mass draws floating paths, the ones nothing pushes, together. Standing on the ground means being held off those paths: that is the push you feel as your weight.

beats.title: Tides
beats.body: High above the Earth, float with one ball inside a small ring. The ball nearest the Earth speeds up a little more, the farthest a little less. So the ring stretches, while its sides draw in. Unlike the ring around the Earth, it holds no mass, so it doesn’t simply shrink. The Moon stretches Earth’s oceans the same way, into two bulges.

scene.why: Curvature is the heart of Einstein’s gravity, and the ocean tides are the part of it you can see.
scene.opening: Two balls are let go side by side, high above the Earth. Nothing pushes either one. Does the gap between them change?

questions.q: Far from any planet, two balls at rest side by side stay the same distance apart. What does it mean if they drift together?
questions.a: Spacetime is curved there: straight paths that start parallel come together, like lines of longitude on a ball.

questions.q: A small ring of floating balls falls toward the Earth. Which way does it stretch?
questions.a: Toward and away from the Earth, while its sides draw in.

questions.q: What makes floating paths around the Earth come together?
